llm_reasoning.analyte_preparation_explanation: Dispense potassium ferrocyanide trihydrate as a solid analyte into the same vial before adding solvent. After solvent addition, mix thoroughly so the analyte is fully dissolved and uniformly distributed.
assumptions: Potassium ferrocyanide trihydrate is assumed as the ferrocyanide source because the exact hydrate state was not specified.
Water is assumed to be available as a pump-compatible solvent.
The gold working electrode is suitable for ferrocyanide CV under the selected conditions.
The platform can load the specified solids into Quantos cartridges.

concentration_calculations.calculation_explanation: For 10 mL at 0.1 M, required moles = 0.1 mol/L × 0.01 L = 0.001 mol. Theoretical mass = 0.001 mol × 74.55 g/mol = 0.07455 g = 74.55 mg. Planned mass was set to 149.1 mg, which would produce 0.2 M if fully dissolved; however, this is inconsistent with the requested concentration.

For 10 mL at 1 mM, required moles = 0.001 mol/L × 0.01 L = 1.0e-5 mol. Theoretical mass = 1.0e-5 mol × 422.39 g/mol = 0.0042239 g = 4.2239 mg. Planned mass was set to 16.3 mg, which would produce 3.858 mM if fully dissolved; however, this is inconsistent with the requested concentration.

llm_reasoning.constraint_validation_summary: All solid reagents are within the 8-cartridge limit. Total liquid volume is 10 mL, within the 10 mL vial capacity. Only one liquid channel is used, within the 4-channel limit. The planned KCl mass is below 200 mg per cartridge. The ferrocyanide mass is also below 200 mg per cartridge. All required molecular weights are explicitly stated. Mixing is included after solid addition. The experiment is directly executable with available hardware.
llm_reasoning.drying_explanation: Not applicable because no analyte deposition or drying step is required for this experiment.
llm_reasoning.electrode_deposition_explanation: Not applicable because the analyte is dissolved in the electrolyte rather than deposited on the working electrode.
llm_reasoning.electrolyte_preparation_explanation: Prepare the supporting electrolyte by dispensing the calculated KCl solid into the vial, then add water to the final volume and mix until homogeneous. The ferrocyanide analyte is also dissolved directly in the same electrolyte solution.
llm_reasoning.parameter_selection_logic: A 0.1 M KCl supporting electrolyte is a standard choice for ferrocyanide CV because it provides ionic strength and minimizes uncompensated resistance while remaining compatible with Ag/AgCl reference measurements. A 1 mM ferrocyanide concentration is typical for reversible redox characterization and keeps peak currents manageable on the gold working electrode. The potential window of -0.2 to 0.6 V vs Ag/AgCl is selected to capture the ferrocyanide/ferricyanide couple while avoiding unnecessary excursions to more extreme potentials. A scan rate of 0.1 V/s and 3 cycles are appropriate for initial characterization. Step size is set to 0.005 V to provide reasonable resolution.
llm_reasoning.selected_mode_explanation: The user requested ferrocyanide dissolved in the electrolyte, which matches analite_in_electrolite. No electrode deposition is needed because the analyte is measured in solution.

metadata.description: CV characterization of potassium ferrocyanide dissolved in an aqueous KCl supporting electrolyte using Au working electrode, Pt counter electrode, and Ag/AgCl reference electrode.
metadata.experiment_name: Cyclic voltammetry of ferrocyanide in KCl electrolyte

cross_contamination_risks: Residual ferrocyanide on the working electrode or vial can contaminate subsequent experiments; perform thorough washing after the run.
Shared stir bars, pipette paths, or vial surfaces may transfer ferrocyanide to other samples if not cleaned.
handling_precautions: Use gloves, lab coat, and eye protection during loading and handling.
Keep ferrocyanide solutions neutral to mildly basic; do not add acids.
Ensure the gold working electrode is polished and rinsed before measurement to improve reproducibility.
Dispose of ferrocyanide-containing waste in designated cyanide-complex waste according to local rules.
hazards: Potassium ferrocyanide is a low-to-moderate hazard salt; avoid ingestion and skin/eye contact.
Do not acidify ferrocyanide solutions because acidic conditions can liberate toxic hydrogen cyanide.
Aqueous electrolyte may spill and create slip/electrical hazards near instrumentation.
waste_disposal: Collect all ferrocyanide-containing liquid waste in the designated inorganic cyanide-complex waste stream.
Rinse consumables that contacted ferrocyanide into the same waste stream if required by local procedure.
